leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Apply the React.ReactNode type to define a component prop that accepts children content.
Implement a component that receives and renders children content through its props interface.
Use the children prop within JSX to display nested content passed from parent components.
Construct parent components that pass JSX elements as children to child components.
Define TypeScript interfaces for components that include an optional children prop with appropriate typing.
Execute conditional rendering logic to control when children content is displayed based on component state.
Utilize the children prop to create reusable wrapper components with consistent styling or behavior.
Access and manipulate children content by using React.Children utility methods when needed.
Modify component structure to accept multiple children elements and render them in specific layouts.
Compare explicit prop passing versus children prop usage for different content composition scenarios.
Return components that properly type and render children content according to TypeScript best practices.
Handle edge cases by implementing default content when no children are provided to a component.
